_meta.indication: For the treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring mesenchymal-epithelial transition (MET) exon 14 skipping alterations.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase II, multicenter, open-label, single-arm study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with metastatic NSCLC whose tumors harbor MET exon 14 skipping alterations, including both treatment-naive and previously treated patients.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (confirmed CR or PR) per RECIST 1.1 as assessed by blinded independent review committee.
pivotal_trials.result: In treatment-naive patients, confirmed ORR per BICR was 43% (95% CI 32, 56) with median DOR 10.8 months (95% CI 6.9, NE). In previously treated patients, confirmed ORR per BICR was 43% (95% CI 33, 55) with median DOR 11.1 months (95% CI 9.5, 18.5).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were edema, fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and dyspnea. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients. Significant/serious identified risks were interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and hepatotoxicity; permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 20% of patients.
target_moa: Tepotinib is a kinase inhibitor that targets MET, including the variant(s) with MET exon 14 skipping alterations.

rems.type: There were no significant safety concerns identified during NDA review requiring risk management beyond labeling or warranting consideration for a REMS.

companion_dx_detail: There is no FDA-approved test for detection of MET exon 14 skipping alterations in NSCLC for selecting patients for treatment with tepotinib; the sponsor agreed to a PMC to support labeling of a companion diagnostic test.

advisory_committee.vote: The division did not refer this application to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions or significant safety or efficacy issues.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to traditional approval for adult patients with metastatic NSCLC harboring MET exon 14 skipping alterations

requirement.text: PMC 4013-4: Submit a summary of the final report of an analytical and clinical validation study to support labeling of an in vitro diagnostic device essential to the safe and effective use of tepotinib in patients with NSCLC whose tumors harbor MET exon 14 skipping.

citations.quote: 4013-4 Submit a summary of the final report of an analytical and clinical validation study, using clinical trial data, that is adequate to support labeling of an in vitro diagnostic device that demonstrates the device is essential to the safe and effective use of tepotinib for patients diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer, whose tumors harbor MET exon 14 skipping. The results of the validation study may inform product labeling.
